newsitem.title: UK: Czech sugar stocks ample to help with damaged beet.
newsitem.headline: Czech sugar stocks ample to help with damaged beet.

text.p: Heavy flooding in the Czech Republic has destroyed some beet fields irreparably but any shortfall in final sugar output can be partly relieved by 1996/97 stocks, E D & F Man said on Monday.
The floods had been described as the worst this century with some fields of crops destroyed in northern Moravia, Man said in its latest report.
"It is difficult to evaluate the ultimate effect on the final sugar outturn at this stage but it seems certain that some beet fields will have been damaged irreparably," the report said.
"Any shortfall in production will be partially alleviated by some carry-over stocks that remain from last year's higher outturn."
Last month Man estimated Czech beet sugar production at 576,000 tonnes for 1996/97, compared with 462,000 tonnes in 1995/96 and 412,000 tonnes the previous year.
Man said farmers in Moravia and also in Poland had been unable to examine the progress of their beet crops, giving rise to speculation of substantial damage.
This had come on top of the 10 percent area reduction in the Czech Republic and one of nine percent in Poland.
"Not only have the floods been localised but the impact on yields is uncertain," the Man report said.
"What is sure is that both countries continue to hold significant surplus stocks which for the time being have been trapped in the respective countries."
The Man report said while Poland had also been affected by the flooding, sugar beet areas were not so severely damaged as in the Czech Republic, with the wheat areas reported to be suffering most.
More than 100 people have been killed in Poland and the Czech Republic after torrential rains in early July caused floods to sweep through the region, costing billions of dollars in damage.
